title: Optical Mapping Preparations for Petunia spp.
author: Elena Hilario
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.baq3idyn
materials: After decanting the last 1X PBS wash, transfer the leaf tissue to the Petri dish containing ~ 4 mL, ice cold NEB complete . Place the Petri dish securely on ice. Finely chop the sample using two scalpel blades, as if they were knife and fork until the pieces are ~ 1 mm.

Discard supernatant and gently resuspend the pellet with 30 mL, ice cold NEB –βME by gently inverting the closed tube. Dispose the supernatant containing β-mercaptoethanol according to your institution's guidelines.

Discard supernatant and gently resuspend the pellet with 30 mL, ice cold NEB –βME by gently inverting the closed tube. Dispose the supernatant containing β-mercaptoethanol according to your institution's guidelines.

steps.title: Tissue Fixation
steps.instruction: Perform tissue fixation in a fume hood.

substeps.instruction: Place ~0.5 g of very young leaves in a 50 mL Falcon tube containing ~45 mL Fixing solution.
Attach a green screened cap and slowly add more Fixing solution to reach a total volume of 60 mL.
Tap the tube while keeping it upright to remove all air bubbles.
Close the tube with its own cap and incubate on ice for 10 minutes.
Discard the Fixing solution by pouring it through the green screened cap (dispose of formaldehyde waste per institutional guidelines).
Add 60 mL of 0.125 M glycine solution through the green screened cap.
Remove air bubbles and incubate on ice at 0 °C for 10 minutes.

steps.title: PBS Wash
steps.instruction: Wash the tissue with PBS solution.

substeps.instruction: Discard the glycine solution through the green screened cap.
Add 60 mL of ice cold 1X PBS solution, remove air bubbles, and incubate on ice at 0 °C for 10 minutes.
Repeat the wash step two more times.

steps.title: Tissue Homogenization
steps.instruction: Homogenize the tissue using one of the following methods:

substeps.instruction: Method A (Homogenizer): Transfer sample and buffer to a tissue homogenizer using a spatula and Pasteur pipette. Add 5-10 mL ice cold NEB complete. Place the homogenizer in an ice bucket (covered up to halfway). Gently grind with the pestle in a spiral movement, keeping the pestle just below the liquid level to avoid foam. Use a pipette to bring sample into medium if tissue sticks to the bottom.

Method B (Liquid Nitrogen): Place tissue on a clean Petri dish and pat dry with lint-free tissue. Transfer to a precooled mortar and freeze with liquid nitrogen. Perform 3 cycles of grind/freeze until a fine powder is obtained. Transfer powder to a 100 mL glass beaker with a magnetic stirrer and 30 mL NEB-complete buffer; stir gently until homogeneous.
Method C: Use a bead beater or TissueLyzer according to instrument instructions.

steps.title: Sample Filtration
steps.instruction: Filter the homogenized sample to remove debris.

substeps.instruction: Place one sheet of Miracloth inside a funnel and place the funnel in a 50 mL Falcon tube.
Pre-wet the Miracloth with 2-3 mL NEB complete and discard the filtered solution.
Filter the homogenized sample through the Miracloth. If flow is slow, gently brush the inside of the sheet with a clean spatula.
Discard the Miracloth sheet and adjust the final volume to 30 mL using ice cold NEB complete.

steps.title: Nuclei Permeabilization
steps.instruction: Permeabilize the nuclei using Triton X-100.

substeps.instruction: Add 600 µL of 25% Triton X-100 by pipetting it in a circular motion against the top of the tube's inside wall.
Close the tube and mix gently by inversion approximately 20 times (final concentration 0.5%).
Centrifuge for 15 minutes at 10 °C to pellet the nuclei.
Discard the supernatant and resuspend the nuclei pellet in 7 mL NEB_A by gently swirling the tube; keep on ice.

steps.title: Percoll Gradient Preparation
steps.instruction: Prepare Percoll gradients while waiting for centrifugations.

substeps.instruction: Prepare 10 mL of 75% Percoll in NEB_A and split equally into two 15 mL Falcon tubes (ensure tubes weigh exactly the same).
Prepare 10 mL of 37.5% Percoll in NEB_A and split equally into two 15 mL Falcon tubes (ensure tubes weigh exactly the same).
Store both sets in the refrigerator until needed.

steps.title: Nuclei Sieving and Washing
steps.instruction: Sieve the nuclei and perform additional washes.

substeps.instruction: Assemble two 50 mL Falcon tubes with 100 µm and 40 µm sieves, respectively, on an ice bucket.
Pour the nuclei suspension through the 100 µm sieve, then through the 40 µm sieve (replace 40 µm sieve if flow slows). Discard sieves and keep sample on ice.
Centrifuge for 15 minutes at 10 °C, discard supernatant, and resuspend the pellet in 7 mL NEB_A.
Repeat the centrifugation and resuspension step three more times.

steps.title: First Percoll Gradient Centrifugation
steps.instruction: Separate nuclei using the 75% Percoll gradient.

substeps.instruction: Carefully overlay 3.5 mL of filtered nuclei suspension over each 75% Percoll solution (ensure loaded tubes weigh exactly the same).
Centrifuge for 30 minutes at 10 °C with acceleration set to 9 (max) and deceleration set to 1 (min).
Using a light source behind the gradient, slowly collect the sample at the interphase with a glass Pasteur pipette.
Transfer the sample to a new 15 mL Falcon tube and keep on ice.

steps.title: Second Percoll Gradient Centrifugation
steps.instruction: Further purify nuclei using the 37.5% Percoll gradient.

substeps.instruction: Carefully overlay half of the collected sample onto each 37.5% Percoll tube (ensure tubes weigh exactly the same).
Centrifuge to collect the nuclei.
Remove the solution with a disposable Pasteur pipette without disturbing the small, pale yellowish nuclei pellet.

steps.title: Final Nuclei Wash and Concentration
steps.instruction: Wash and concentrate the nuclei pellets.

substeps.instruction: Resuspend each nuclei pellet in 10 mL NEB_B.
Centrifuge for 30 minutes at 10 °C with both acceleration and deceleration set to 9 (max).
Remove the solution with a Pasteur pipette, leaving ~200 µL of solution.
Gently tap the bottom of the tube to resuspend nuclei and transfer to a 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tube. Repeat for the second pellet.
Add ~600 µL NEB_B and spin down at 6,000 rpm for 1 minute at room temperature.
Discard 600 µL supernatant and resuspend nuclei in the remaining 400 µL NEB_B by tapping the bottom of the tube; keep on ice.
Place CleanCut 2% Agarose bottle in a 70 °C water bath. Once melted, transfer 400 µL to a screw-capped tube and keep in the water bath.
Precool a strip of disposable plug molds on Parafilm over an ice bucket.
Incubate the nuclei and the melted 2% agarose at 43 °C for 10 minutes.
Transfer the nuclei mix to the agarose tube and mix very gently by pipetting in and out until even.
Place the precooled plug mold on a paper towel on the bench.
Dispense ~90 µL per plug (prepare ~8 plugs). Cool completely at 0 °C for 10 minutes.

steps.title: Proteinase K Digestion and Washing
steps.instruction: Digest and wash the agarose plugs.

substeps.instruction: Pop the agarose plugs into Proteinase K lysis mix and incubate at 50 °C for 20 hours without shaking.
Wash plugs in 25 mL Wash-1 at 50 °C for 1 hour without shaking.
Wash plugs in 25 mL Wash-2 at 20 °C for 1 hour in a rotisserie at the slowest speed (tube placed horizontally).
Store each plug in ~2 mL Wash-2 in screw-capped tubes at 4 °C, avoiding air bubbles.

steps.title: PFGE Analysis
steps.instruction: Analyze the plugs using Pulsed-Field Gel Electrophoresis (PFGE).

substeps.instruction: Use a 1% agarose gel (Certified Megabase Agarose BioRad) in 1X TAE.
Apply settings: 60-120", 120°, 6 V/cm, 15 °C, for 24 hours.
Stain the gel with SYBR Safe.
